bottom_low_issuance.label: Bottom 50 worth $2B+ on dilution alone (heaviest issuers)

verdict: Rebalanced every quarter for 14 years. Top 30 worth $10B+: +13.5% a year against SPY's +15.6% (behind by 2.1), beat SPY in 49% of quarters (t = -0.8: could be luck). Top 50 worth $2B+: +15.7% a year against SPY's +15.6% (ahead by 0.1), beat SPY in 56% of quarters (t = 0.3: could be luck). Top 50 worth $300M-$10B, no flaws: +16.9% a year against SPY's +15.6% (ahead by 1.4), beat SPY in 56% of quarters (t = 0.8: could be luck). The average screened stock, equal-weighted, made +14.2% a year, so beating SPY at all took picking well; the bottom 50 trailed SPY by 0.8 points a quarter (t = -0.7: could be luck). Of the four grades alone, the worst on momentum lagged most (-1.5 points a quarter). The worst on value alone led SPY (+1.0 a quarter): in this period that grade pointed the wrong way. Survivorship: up to 32% of large SEC filers from those dates have no ticker today and are missing, which flatters the buy lists and, since the missing are more often failures, understates how badly the bottom did.
